issues.description: DescriptorProto() silently returns nil on empty files instead of guarding the zero-case path
issues.detail: `(*imports).DescriptorProto()` now returns nil when `i == nil`, but on a non-nil but empty `imports` it still calls `slicesx.Last(i.files)` and returns `imported.file` (likely nil) without indicating absence. The zero-test only checks no-panic; it doesn't check that the contract makes sense. If empty files is reachable, the caller gets a nil File and the existing `IsDescriptorProto` nil-guard papers over it. State the invariant or document the nil-return.

issues.description: Same nil-then-call-method pattern copy-pasted across 15+ accessors; this should be one helper or a method on the zero receiver
issues.detail: Every accessor on `*File` and `Type` now has the same five-line `var x T; if f != nil { x = f.field }; return wrap(x, ...)` shape. That's THREE-PATCHES worth of duplication smeared into one. The right shape is either methods that work on nil receivers directly (Go allows this) or one `safeSlice` helper. Fifteen near-identical blocks is a maintainer-tax patch.

issues.description: Patch bundles 'fix panics on zero values' with 'add zero test' — these are two patches
issues.detail: Commit message admits two things: add the test, and fix the panics it surfaces. When this regresses in a year, bisect lands on a commit that does both and the reviewer has to reread 200 lines to find which production change broke something. Split: one patch adds the test (red), then per-package patches make it green. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: Reflection-driven test is clever where table-driven would be obvious and debuggable
issues.detail: `testZeroAny` walks `reflect.Method`, special-cases `IsZero`/`Context`/`ValueNodeIndex` by name, and asserts `r.Interface()` is zero. When this fails six months from now on a new accessor, the failure message is `non-zero return #0 of ir.Foo.Bar` and the maintainer has to mentally simulate reflect. A table of `{name, fn func(T) any}` is uglier in line-count but trivially debuggable. Borderline BAD-TASTE.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex returning -1 as a sentinel is a new special case the test then has to special-case
issues.detail: `Element.ValueNodeIndex()` returns -1 on zero, and `testZeroAny` has a dedicated branch for that method name. That's a special case adding a special case — exactly the BAD-TASTE pattern. Either the zero element has no valid index (return 0 and document it as undefined when IsZero), or the API should return `(int, bool)`. The -1 sentinel will leak into callers.

issues.description: Symbol.RawData() in export_test.go silently returns Nil instead of letting test catch the real bug
issues.detail: Test-only helper now returns `arena.Nil()` for zero Symbols. If a test passes a zero Symbol where it shouldn't, you've masked it instead of letting it panic loudly. Test infrastructure should fail fast on garbage input, not normalize it. Either make this a real `Symbol.RawData()` on the type, or leave the panic and fix the caller.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The intent is right — zero-value accessors shouldn't panic, and a regression test for that contract is good hygiene. But the execution is two patches stapled together (add test + fix panics), with fifteen copies of the same nil-guard boilerplate that wants to be one helper or nil-receiver methods. The reflection-based test is clever where a table would be obvious, and the new -1 sentinel from ValueNodeIndex adds a special case the test then has to special-case. Split it, dedupe the guards, reconsider the sentinel.
